U.S. Hiring Strengthens.
subject: New Zealand Counts. Iran Mediation Continues. U.S. Hiring Strengthens.
preview_text: A close vote, Gulf diplomacy and U.S. jobs, plus the rest of the world in six minutes.
description: New Zealand faces a close count, Qatar keeps Iran mediation active and stronger U.S. hiring complicates the economic outlook.
contents_extra: Kyiv’s infrastructure, global updates, trivia and your poll

stories.title: New Zealand’s Close Count Puts Coalition Arithmetic in Focus
paragraphs: New Zealand’s National and Labour parties were close in Saturday’s preliminary election count. Reuters reported a narrow National lead as the first results arrived. In later reporting checked at 11:14:36 UTC, the governing coalition retained a slim projected advantage. No final result or government agreement was established.

Al Jazeera reports that the centrist Opportunity Party crossed the 5% threshold in preliminary results. Its performance could matter if coalition negotiations are required. The election focused heavily on living costs, including grocery prices. Final results, including overseas ballots, are expected Nov. 27, so the seat picture remains provisional.

stories.title: Qatar Says Iran Mediation Continues After New U.S. Strikes
paragraphs: Qatar said efforts to contain the Iran conflict remained active Saturday, rejecting reports that negotiations had collapsed. Al Jazeera reports that its foreign ministry disputed those claims. The statement followed Trump’s confirmation of new U.S. strikes against Iranian air defenses and Iranian reports of explosions on Qeshm Island.

The island sits beside the Strait of Hormuz, an important route for global oil shipments. AP reports that Trump offered limited detail about the latest target. Gulf governments have continued diplomatic calls. Public claims of progress should not be confused with a negotiated settlement, which has not been announced.

stories.title: U.S. Hiring Improves While Canada’s Labor Market Weakens
paragraphs: New employment figures show contrasting conditions in North America. The United States added 165,000 jobs in October and unemployment fell to 4.1%. Reuters reports that earlier U.S. hiring totals were also revised upward. The stronger figures leave the Federal Reserve weighing labor market resilience against inflation and household financial pressure.

Canada, meanwhile, lost a net 4,700 jobs and its unemployment rate rose to 6.7%. Reuters reports weakness in private sector and full time employment. Canada’s economy had lost 46,000 jobs overall this year. The separate U.S. report showed more people entering the labor force, despite its lower unemployment rate.

deep_dive.title: Kyiv’s New Infrastructure Damage Tests the Space for Talks
paragraphs: Russian attacks hit Kyiv and surrounding areas overnight before another planned round of talks. Reuters reports damage to residential buildings and a kindergarten building, citing Ukrainian officials. Subsequent reporting described strikes affecting a major bridge and energy infrastructure. The attacks continued despite diplomatic preparations, leaving civilian protection an immediate concern separate from negotiations over a settlement.

The practical effects extend beyond individual impact sites. DW reports that Kyiv’s mayor described serious difficulties with electricity, heating and water. Overnight temperatures fell to freezing. Damage to energy systems can therefore affect households far from a strike location. Ukrainian officials have appealed for more support as they prepare for further attacks on infrastructure.

Russia’s Defense Ministry said the bridge carried weapons and that a targeted plant produced missiles. DW attributes those descriptions to Moscow; they are not independent verification of the targets’ use. Al Jazeera reports that Ukrainian officials described damage to civilian buildings. The competing accounts require clear attribution rather than treating either side’s claims as an established account.

Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States are expected in Abu Dhabi Tuesday. Al Jazeera reports that Ukraine is seeking concrete security guarantees from its partners. Talks among allies in Brussels also addressed reconstruction and funding for next year. DW reports that territorial and security questions have prevented earlier rounds from achieving a breakthrough.

trivia.question: What vote share threshold generally gives a party entry to New Zealand’s parliament?
trivia.explanation: D. 5%. Al Jazeera reports that the Opportunity Party crossed that threshold in preliminary results.

poll.question: Should New Zealand’s next government prioritize the cost of groceries?

World view: Paraguay’s leadership changes. Former Vice President Pedro Alliana took office after the Senate removed Santiago Peña over a bank scandal; Reuters reports.
European media face threats. Broadcasters evacuated buildings and suspended some programs; no bombs were found at the affected sites; Reuters reports.
São Paulo rescue completed. All 35 people inside a collapsed commercial building were rescued, with four taken to hospitals in stable condition; Reuters reports.
Need to know: Measles infections exceed 5,000. The latest U.S. CDC figures count 5,182 cases so far this year; Al Jazeera reports.
A doctor returns for Ebola treatment. A British doctor came home from Congo; authorities said the risk to the wider public remained low; Reuters reports.
Germany detects bird flu. An infected wild goose in Brandenburg prompted a reminder to poultry farmers about biosecurity; Reuters reports.
Money & markets: Technology shares regain ground. The Nasdaq rose about 1.1% Friday, although major U.S. indexes still ended the week lower; Reuters reports.
Lilly expands direct access. A new agreement lets Hims & Hers sell Lilly obesity medicines on its own platform; Reuters reports.
Dental company plans U.S. listing. Swiss startup vVardis seeks a valuation of up to $4.37 billion in its planned offering; Reuters reports.
Future frontiers: Rocket engine deal signed. Firefly’s agreement with AST SpaceMobile supports the planned Blacklift rocket and includes future manufacturing rights; Reuters reports.
Octopuses navigate confined spaces. New research maps how the animals alter their movements as openings shrink; Reuters reports.
China sets Antarctic rules. Beijing approved legislation regulating research, exploration and environmental protection; Reuters reports.
The score: Los Angeles wins 124 to 118. The Lakers beat Portland behind 53 points from Luka Doncic; AP reports.
Arizona wins 29 to 28. A late field goal completed the Wildcats’ comeback against TCU; AP reports.
UConn wins 85 to 77. The Huskies beat Michigan in a rematch of the NCAA championship game; AP reports.
Life & culture: A decade of displacement on film. One in a Million traces a Syrian refugee’s life from childhood in Turkey to settlement in Germany; Reuters reports.
Matsumoto enters the monster story. Godzilla Minus Zero fulfills director Takashi Yamazaki’s wish to feature his hometown; Reuters reports.
Club Kid marks a first. Jordan Firstman’s directorial debut aims to show a more emotionally open side of its creator; Reuters reports.
